title: The Corpus Data Model: Visual Guide
outline: Title: The Corpus Data Model: Visual Guide

1. Four Grains, One Chain | document, document_version, chunk and embedding as separate grains with their columns, plus four upgrade events showing which layers must be rebuilt | separate identities let a pipeline invalidate only the affected descendants, so an embedding-model upgrade touches vectors and never invents new source documents

2. What A Chunk Costs | window and stride sliders over a 6,000-token document showing chunk count, vectors, tokens per hit and whether the deciding clause survives a boundary | chunking sets the retrieval grain and therefore recall, citation precision, vector count and token cost, and changing it is a schema migration

3. Identity Under Change | one sentence inserted at the top of a document, with chunk ids derived from ordinal versus from version, config, offsets and content | ordinal-based ids rename every chunk after any edit, while content-derived ids keep unchanged text stable and make the upsert idempotent

4. The Hash Recipe | three canonicalization rules toggled over two versions of a code snippet, showing when the hashes collide, plus the domain-separated id recipe | a content hash is evidence of equality only under a recorded canonicalization rule, and every derived id needs a type tag and structured input

5. Tracing A Citation | the embedding to chunk to version to document path with offsets and page anchors, plus four ways the chain breaks | lineage is what turns a retrieved chunk into a verifiable citation and makes targeted repair and deletion possible, but it proves origin rather than correctness
